notes: The door is already down and the Major has already given his order; the whole scene is the minute in which the housekeeper has not yet obeyed it, with the tallow stub an arm's length from her apron and Fairbrother's candle watching from the back stair. Obedience sends her below by the back stairs toward S_N02; defiance walks her into the study under the Major's eye and into the Keyhole Filled line.
opening: The study door lies in two pieces across its own threshold, the hall poker beside it where Mr Yardley let it fall, and the master sits at his desk inside as though the room had simply stopped around him: window frozen shut, grate gone to ash, and in the mantel candlestick, among the white wax, a yellow tallow stub snuffed down to nothing. Major Carrington, the key that was heard to fall to the carpet already in his coat pocket, has given his order to the housekeeper, 'Below, and count the plate,' and turned his back on it to bend over the desk with Doctor Ashcombe. Fairbrother stands on the back stair with his candle held low and says, not quite to you, 'A housekeeper's place is below, ma'am, when gentlemen are in a room; the hall remembers who forgot it.' Along the gallery the guests' doors stand open and the maids crowd the stair head, and nobody has yet left the doorway the Major pointed from.

variants.text: The broken door has been propped against the linen press. Through the gap the Major stands between you and the desk, and the mantel candlestick is behind his shoulder.
Bare boards, the fire bucket kicked over in the rush, the end window white with frost to its upper pane. The study door lies in two pieces and the room beyond it is colder than the landing.
Fairbrother's candle waits at the head of the back stair, held low for a servant's feet, as he has held it for forty years of other people's.
The back stair is dark. Fairbrother has gone down with his candle and left no light behind him, which in this house is a sentence.
From the study end the Major's voice carries: '...the housekeeper will see to it.' Flat, but a title, and said where the maids can hear.
From the study end the Major's voice carries: '...that woman.' Loud enough to be meant for the gallery, and the maids on the stair hear it too.
Grey snow light through the half-landing window. The barometer has stood at Stormy for two days and the maids stand at the newel post in their nightcaps, not sent down by anyone.

The doors along the gallery are closing one by one, the widow's last. Mr Yardley stands on the Turkey runner with the poker he has picked up again, as if he does not know whose hand it belongs in now.
Every door on the gallery stands open and every sconce is lit; the Turkey runner is rucked where the household ran along it. The waxwings watch from their case with glass eyes.

options.detail: 'I came up about the fire, sir. For the doctor.'
options.label: 'About the fire, sir. For the doctor.'
options.text: The Major straightens, finds you in the doorway, and takes the excuse as he would from a footman: a nod toward the back stair, and his attention gone back to the desk before you have turned. He does not watch you go. Fairbrother does.

options.detail: 'Sir, the key that fell. Where is it now?'
options.label: 'The key that fell, sir. Where is it?'
options.text: Doctor Ashcombe's hands stop on the master's collar. The Major's hand goes to his coat pocket and stays there, closed over it. 'The housekeeper is new, Ashcombe,' he says to the doctor, not to you. 'She will learn what is asked of her.' The doctor does not turn round, but he has heard.

options.label: palm the tallow stub into your apron
options.text: Two steps on the bare boards, the stub cold and greasy between finger and thumb, and either it is in your apron pocket before the Major turns, or Fairbrother's eyes on the back stair go to your hand and the Major, straightening, follows them to the empty socket among the white wax.

options.detail: 'Is there anything to be brought up, Doctor?'
options.label: 'Anything to be brought up, Doctor?'
options.text: 'A sheet,' the doctor says, without turning. 'And hot water, though it will do him no good.' The Major does not look up; the stub stays where it is.

actions.label: down the back stairs to the plate
actions.text: You go down as ordered, past Fairbrother at the turn of the back stair. He is setting the tallow box square to the edge of its shelf without looking inside it, as he must have done ten thousand nights; he has counted it already, and you can see that in how he does not count it now. Below, the plate waits in its baize, and above, the keyhole.

actions.detail: the four walls, key ring in fist
actions.label: refuse the Major: walk the four walls
actions.text: 'I will see the room, sir, before it is shut.' You step over the broken door with the key ring closed in your fist and walk the four walls while the Major argues at your back: the poker straight in its stand, the window frozen in its frame, the ash cold, and the yellow tallow stub in the white-wax candlestick, each said aloud and carried out to the gallery where the whole house is listening. Fairbrother's candle goes down the back stair without you, and the maids on the stair head hear him tell them what the new woman has forgotten.

events.text: Mr Yardley comes along the gallery with the poker still in his hand, sets it in the fire bucket at the study end, looks at it there, and takes it up again. 'Someone should wire the police,' he says, and then remembers the snow.
The doctor straightens from the desk and says, to the room, that the master has been dead some hours, and that the window has been frozen shut longer than that.

nudges.text: Major Carrington's voice, carrying through the house: 'Housekeeper. The plate. I gave an order.'
A draught moves through the house and every flame leans with it; somewhere below, a door Fairbrother would ordinarily have shut bangs once and is still.

props.name: the yellow tallow stub
props.description: A finger's length of cheap yellow tallow, snuffed hard, standing in the study's mantel candlestick among the white wax that is all the master ever burned. It is the servants' candle; the box it came from is on a shelf at the foot of the back stair.

frame.composition: Eye-level shot from the study end landing, framed through the splintered doorway with the broken door lying across the threshold in the foreground
subjects: Major Carrington in a dressing gown bent over the desk, one hand flat on his coat pocket
Doctor Ashcombe beside him with his back to the door, hands at the dead master's collar
the master slumped at the desk, grey, unmoving
Reginald Fairbrother on the back stair to one side, candle held low, face lit from below, watching the doorway
a small yellow tallow stub in a brass candlestick among tall white wax on the mantel
frame.environment: Before dawn in a snowbound Victorian country house; grey-blue snow light through a window white with frost, a single candle and a guttering oil lamp the only warm light, a dead grate, breath visible in the cold
frame.palette_mood: Cold grey-blue and frost white against small pools of tallow yellow and lamp amber; dark panelling, deep shadow; hushed, suspended, watchful
